entities.text: G. Thirupathi Goud vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners filed this writ petition questioning the action of respondent Nos.2 to 4 in trying to dispossess them from their agricultural land to an extent of each Ac.2.12 gts. in Sy.No.59/14//1 and Sy.No.59/14//3 situated at Chinthala Manepalli Village and Mandal, Komrambheem Asifabad District, (for short, 'the subject property') without initiating the proceedings as required under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (Act No.30 of 2013) (hereinafter referred to, as 'the Act'), and the same is contrary to the provisions of the Act and in violation of Article 300-A of the Constitution of India.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
2. Heard Mr. K. Venumadhav, learned counsel for the petitioners, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Irrigation appearing for respondent No.1 and Ms. T. Swetcha, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue appearing for respondent Nos.2 to 4.
3.

Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Irrigation, basing on the instructions furnished by the Executive Engineer, I & CADD, Irrigation Division No.3, Kaghaznagar, Kumurambheem Asifabad District, vide Letter No.EE/IRRGN/ID- 3/DEE(T)/AEE/KZNR/550/M dated 28.02.2025,
submitted that respondent Nos. 2 to 4 are not interfering with the subject property of the petitioners.

However, if the land of the petitioners is required for acquisition for the public purpose,
they will follow the due process as contemplated under the provisions of the Act.

4. Taking into consideration the submissions made by the learned Assistant Government, without expressing any view on the merits of the case, respondent Nos.2 to 4 are directed to not to dispossess the petitioners from the subject property without following due process of law.
5. With the above direction, the writ petition is disposed of.
Miscellaneous petitions, pending if any, shall stand closed.

__ J. SREENIVAS RAO, J Date: 04.03.2025 mar G. Thirupathi Goud vs The State Of Telangana, on 4 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116007828/
